purpose: Assemble expert perspectives to guide background literature search for 'Mapping the Moral Mind of Machines' paper

members.expertise: MFT's adoption in NLP, MFTC lineage, computational moral language analysis
members.search_guidance: Track the Haidt→Graham→Hoover→Abdulhai citation chain. Look for papers that explain WHY MFT became the default framework in NLP (circa 2018-2020). Key venues: ACL, EMNLP, NAACL. Also find the early moral sentiment analysis papers that preceded MFT adoption.

members.expertise: Greene's fMRI studies, cognitive load effects, utilitarian vs deontological processing
members.search_guidance: Find Greene's foundational fMRI papers (2001, 2004, 2009), the personal vs impersonal dilemma distinction, cognitive load manipulation studies, and recent LLM papers that test dual-process predictions without naming the theory. Also look for Cushman's work on model-free vs model-based moral cognition.

members.expertise: Haidt's intuitionism, moral dumbfounding, emotion-first moral judgment
members.search_guidance: Start with Haidt 2001 ('The Emotional Dog'), find moral dumbfounding experiments (Haidt et al. 2000, Royzman & Bonanno), the elephant/rider metaphor papers, and any attempt to test post-hoc rationalization in AI. Key concept: reasoning as 'press secretary' not 'judge'.

members.expertise: Gray & Schein's theory, agent-patient dynamics, harm perception
members.search_guidance: Find Gray et al. 2012 (original theory), Schein & Gray 2018 (Theory of Dyadic Morality), papers on moral typecasting (agents judged as intentional, patients as suffering), and any computational operationalization. Also look for the 'harm as essence of morality' debate.

members.expertise: Schwartz Value Theory, World Values Survey, WEIRD critique
members.search_guidance: Find Schwartz 1992/2012 (theory + refined theory), PVQ-40 and PVQ-RR validation studies, Henrich et al. 2010 (WEIRD critique), and cross-cultural LLM value studies. Look for papers comparing Western vs non-Western moral frameworks in AI.

members.expertise: Kohlberg's stages, Rest's DIT, moral development measurement
members.search_guidance: Find Rest 1979 (DIT manual), Thoma 2006 (DIT-2 update), the massive DIT meta-analyses (Bebeau & Thoma), and any LLM moral development papers. DIT has 40+ years of norms — find the key validation papers.

members.expertise: Construct validity, measurement invariance, instrument revalidation
members.search_guidance: Find Messick 1995 (validity evidence framework), papers on measurement invariance when changing respondent populations, any work on revalidating human instruments for AI (a very new area). Also look for Cronbach & Meehl 1955 (construct validity original).

members.expertise: LLM evaluation methodology, benchmark quality meta-analyses
members.search_guidance: Find HELM (Liang et al. 2023), BIG-bench (Srivastava et al. 2023), benchmark contamination studies, and recent meta-surveys of LLM ethics evaluation. Look for papers critiquing benchmark quality or proposing evaluation frameworks.

Find Ouyang et al. 2022 (InstructGPT), Bai et al. 2022 (Constitutional AI), papers on how RLHF shapes moral outputs, and the debate about whether alignment training creates genuine moral understanding vs surface compliance.

members.expertise: Survey design for LLMs, prompting effects on responses
members.search_guidance: Find Santurkar et al. 2023 (opinion survey reliability), Argyle et al. 2023 (silicon sampling), papers on Likert scale bias in LLMs, response distribution studies, and persona/role-playing effects on moral responses.

members.role: Philosophy of Mind / AI Ethics Scholar
members.expertise: Moral agency, moral competence, philosophical grounding
members.search_guidance: Find papers on whether LLMs can be moral agents (Floridi, Coeckelbergh), the moral Turing test concept, and philosophical analyses of what it means to 'measure morality' in machines. Also: Gabriel et al. 2026 Nature roadmap.

members.expertise: Benchmark reproducibility, open science, replication crisis
members.search_guidance: Find papers on the replication crisis in AI benchmarks, benchmark contamination, evaluation gaming, and standards for reproducible moral evaluation. Look for Biderman et al., Dehghani et al. on data documentation.

members.expertise: Cross-lingual moral evaluation, video/image moral reasoning
members.search_guidance: Find papers on multilingual moral benchmarks, value assessment in non-English languages, and multimodal moral reasoning (e.g., Value-Spectrum video VQA). Look for cultural bias in English-centric moral evaluation.
